messages.author: ac1099cfd4f2b3f2
messages.subject: Assumed genotyping error
parts:
Hi

I called SNPs using tassel from a mapping population using GBS data (96-plex) sequenced at Cornell . Now I am using R/qtl for the linkage map contruction, some of the steps ask me for a value about an Assumed genotyping error. Does anyone else know about which value to use for GBS data?

Thank you in advance

messages.author: 96353e7106735838
messages.subject: Re: Assumed genotyping error
parts:
Ideally use an assumed genotyping error rate that approximately matches the actual error rate.

It generally has little influence on the inference of marker order, but can affect the estimates of inter-marker distances. I had generally used 0.01 for old low-density microsat data and am now generally using 0.002 for SNP arrays, but I've not worked with GBS data directly. I'd try out different values and see how different the results are. And you can in principle estimate the error rate. See pg 35 of the genetic map construction tutorial: http://rqtl.org/tutorials/geneticmaps.pdf

karl
